messages:
Cameron: Heads up — noticed a big main-thread stall on canary this morning. Charts (metric-grid + heatmap) freeze ~600ms more than before the runtime bump.

Cameron: Wall-clock: 95th p75 -> p95 jump around 08:12 UTC, but only on canary users (10% route). Screenshot + flame: https://img.redwood.fake/6854321000/flame.png

Anya: Ugh. Any recent client-side rollout? bundle sizes or chunk ids? :eyes:

Cameron: We shipped runtime@2.4.1 and a webpack config tweak in frontend-pack that changes deterministicChunkIds -> natural to get smaller names (PR #8135). Not sure if that can affect caching.

Sergio: natural ids could break cacheability across deploys if the module graph order changed. That leads to cache misses and repeated parser/parse+compile on client. Do you have har or network waterfall?

Cameron: Quick HAR attached: repeated fetch for main-chunk.js with 200s but Content-Length is the same, yet we see parse spikes. Copy of waterfall: (snip)

Cameron: small log snippet from client console when it hangs: 
```
[perf] parse-main 84ms
[perf] eval-main 410ms
[perf] long-task 620ms
```

Maria: I just checked the CDN dashboard — a deploy earlier today toggled Cache-Control on our build assets to `no-cache, no-store` because of a mistaken purge flag in the pipeline. That would force revalidation for everyone. Rolling assets + natural ids = thrash.

Lee: So likely two orthogonal changes combined: chunk id scheme + CDN header TTL -> client keeps re-downloading slightly different named assets and repeatedly parsing them.

Anya: Can we confirm that the requests have differing ETags or query strings? If ETag changes, we know it's new content.

Cameron: Inspecting responses: ETag present but `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store`. So browser still does conditional GETs and re-parses on 200 responses.

Sergio: Reverting deterministic->natural is low-risk. Maria — can you flip the CDN header back to `max-age=604800` for static assets? That would buy time.

Maria: On it. Patching CDN edge policy now. ETA ~5m.

DeployBot: deploy/frontend-pack@canary started by @maria (sha: ab12cd)

Cameron: After Maria's change I'm seeing far fewer fetches, p95 main-thread dropped ~450ms within 2 mins. Looks promising.

Lee: Long-term: we should not change chunk id semantics without a coordinated asset-versioning plan. Two suggestions: 1) enforce deterministic ids for production bundles, 2) add a post-build step that stamps a stable manifest used by the router for canary routing.

Anya: We should also add a telemetry event for repeated revalidation of main-chunk within X seconds (counts >2) so we can alert next time.

Sergio: Agree. I'll open an RFC for chunk-id policy + a small check in the CI that fails if CDN headers are unset for assets.

Cameron: Action items: Maria — CDN header rollback (done), Sergio — RFC + CI check (assigned), Anya — telemetry event (assigned), Lee — review canary routing to ensure pods reuse warm Vary headers. I'll monitor canary for 2 hours and report back. :thumbsup:

Maria: CDN change rolled, canary metrics improving. Will follow up if anything pops. :white_check_mark:

DeployBot: deploy/frontend-pack@canary finished successfully (duration: 1m 12s)

Cameron: Thanks all — closing this thread once the 2hr drift stays down. If anyone sees renewed spikes ping here.

Lee: filed follow-up tickets: FE-948 (chunk-id policy), INF-212 (cdn-header-ci).

Anya: I'll add the telemetry hook to the alert playbook.

Sergio: RFC draft up at https://go.redwood.fake/rfc/chunk-ids — please review.
